title: Measurement: setup spends nothing before it has to, asks separately for the one check that costs money, and reports readiness from the record it read back
summary: TSK-0060 SLICE 4, toward ACC-0045 and — not yet evaluated — ACC-0043, ACC-0085, ACC-0106, ACC-0107, ACC-0108. The implementation is commit 7d0d48a; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. THE ORDER IS WHAT THIS SLICE IS ABOUT. After the research decision, three declared phases run: `preflight`, `live-check` and `read-back`. The preflight is `zeroCostPreflight`, which settles everything a run can be refused for without spending anything — the committed selection, this host's grant for it, the credential contract, Pi's catalogue, the thinking level that model supports, and the package — and sends nothing. Only then is the one check that costs money offered. THE BILLABLE CHECK HAS ITS OWN ANSWER, SEPARATE FROM EVERY OTHER ONE. `--live-model-check approve|deny` settles it without a prompt; interactively the operator is asked, with the prompt naming the provider, the exact model and that the provider may charge; and a run with nobody to ask refuses rather than assuming, which reaches the operator as a partial setup rather than as a fault. A decline leaves the project valid, the model committed and nothing recorded. READINESS IS WHAT THE RECORD SAYS ON DISK. The live check writes the compatibility record; a separate phase reads it back and compares it against the key recomputed from what Pi resolved in this run. That is not ceremony: the gate that refuses a tracked or unprotected record applies on READ as well as on write, so a record that cannot be read back is one the next start will refuse, and reporting readiness from the writer's return value would be a promise about somebody else's next run. What the command prints comes from the record that was read. THREE DEFECTS FOUND IN REVIEW, AND WHAT THEY WERE (0caaf7b, eeb79bc). FIRST, the canary was given no stored credential path, so its child ran against an empty store: a model Pi authenticates from its saved auth.json would have failed a check that was never handed what makes it work. The request now carries the path, and only when the preflight found the stored file is the source that authenticates this selection — because the canary refuses a stored path that is not there, and an environment-authenticated host commonly has no auth.json at all. Passing it narrows rather than widens: the canary copies the selected provider's entry alone into its isolated root, a boundary measured in test/pi-provider-canary.test.mjs. SECOND, the recovery read trusted a file too early. It is now contained before the first byte — the state root must resolve inside the canonical project root, and the journal inside that as a regular file, so a link on `.pi` or on `.pi/runtime` is refused rather than followed — validated against its schema before any field is used, and never the source of what is printed: the command the operator is told to run is built from this run's own project path. THIRD, that command quoted spaces and printed `C:/a&b/project` bare, which splits a command line in two — and then, on the first correction, used double quotes on Windows, which PowerShell expands: `"C:/a$null/project"` arrives as `C:/a/project`, a different directory with nothing to notice. The command now targets PowerShell explicitly and says so, quoting every path in single quotes with an apostrophe written twice, and the control runs the generated line through that shell against paths holding `$`, a backtick, `&` and an apostrophe, reading back which project the command actually reached. It is recomputed from this run's own project path in every case, never taken from the journal. AN INTERRUPTED RUN IS CONTINUED DELIBERATELY. The journal's presence is the interruption signal. An ordinary rerun names the last completed phase, prints the recovery command the interrupted run itself recorded, and exits 10 having changed nothing; `--resume` continues, and a completed run leaves no journal. `--resume` with nothing to resume says so and proceeds as an ordinary run. THE EXIT CODES ARE PUBLISHED. `--help` prints every code with what it means, and a test holds each member of the command's own EXIT table to having both a published meaning and a line in that output. This slice adds two: 10 for an interrupted run, and 11 for a model that was not shown to work — which is deliberately distinct from 9, the code for an answer that left setup partial, because a script has to tell a decline from a failure. MEASURED THROUGH THE REAL COMMAND. (1) A zero-cost refusal leaves `live-check` and `read-back` PENDING in the journal the failed run left, with the canary never called. (2) A denied check, a declined one and one nobody could approve each send nothing and record nothing, with the model still committed and the scaffold valid. (3) A passing check is recorded, read back, and reused by the next run: no question, no request, and the record's bytes unchanged. (4) A check that returns not-passed, and one that passes while proving a different endpoint, are both refused with nothing recorded. (5) The read-back itself refuses a record that is gone and one about another model. (6) The interruption, the resume and the no-op resume are all exercised on a real journal. NOTHING BILLABLE IS REACHED, AND THAT IS ENFORCED BY THE FIXTURE. The canary is the single step that sends a request to the selected provider, and the fixture's model is a real OpenAI catalogue entry, so every case injects its own runner; the default — the real canary — is never reached in a test. The injected runner returns what a passing check would have observed, derived from the preflight the command itself resolved, which is also what makes the key comparison meaningful rather than circular. LIMITS. One mutation survives: swallowing a preflight refusal. In this fixture an earlier zero-cost phase refuses first — when the host's stored key goes, its only remaining provider is the loopback one, which has no credential contract — so setup's own tests cannot distinguish a preflight that refuses from one that is ignored. The preflight's individual refusals are held by test/launch-checks.test.mjs. Also unchanged from the earlier slices: R9's alternate content root, custom-provider credential inputs (D25, D13) and `--local-state user` are all still owed, and the spanning criteria stay not-evaluated until they land and the integration record is written. The per-class exit codes are published, but several refusal classes still share the generic setup code; narrowing those is the rest of that mapping. CI. GitHub Actions run 35870095611 at bcfd79a — the slice's final commit — attempt 1 with no job re-run, passed in all four cells, with the setup command's 36 tests running in every cell; the live compatibility tier ran in the ubuntu Node 24 cell and passed 6 of 6. Every earlier commit of the slice passed all four cells too. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Twenty-one changes across four sets, each restored byte-identical by sha256. Twenty were caught: the read-back skipped, a not-ready check reported as ready, a declined check and a failed one sharing a code, an unapproved check assumed approved, the canary given no preflight, an interrupted run continued without being asked, the read-back accepting a record about another model, the read-back accepting an unreadable record, the canary given no saved credential, the canary handed the wrong store, the journal read without containment, a non-file at the journal path read, the journal used unvalidated, the printed recovery command taken from the file, a path with spaces left unquoted, the state root not checked against the project, quoting applied only to paths that look awkward, POSIX given Windows quoting, a stored path supplied whatever authenticates, and no stored path supplied at all. THE ONE THAT SURVIVES is swallowing a preflight refusal, for the reason stated above.

facts.implementation: commits 7d0d48a (slice 4), 0caaf7b, eeb79bc and bcfd79a (the review fixes)
facts.tests: test/setup-command.test.mjs: 36 tests, 25 of which run the real main(); one runs it in a child with every access recorded, and the rest hold exported functions directly.
facts.phases: preflight, live-check and read-back, declared and run in that order after the research decision
facts.zero-cost-first: a zero-cost refusal leaves live-check and read-back pending in the journal, with the canary never called
facts.separate-approval: --live-model-check approve|deny, an interactive question naming the provider, the model and that it may be charged, or a refusal when there is nobody to ask; a decline records nothing and sends nothing
facts.read-back: the record is re-read and compared against the key recomputed from what Pi resolved; a missing record and one about another model are both refused as not-proved
facts.reuse: a second run reuses the recorded check without asking, without sending, and without rewriting the record's bytes
facts.failed-check: a not-passed canary and one that proves a different endpoint are both refused with nothing recorded
facts.resume: an ordinary rerun after an interruption exits 10 naming the last completed phase and the recorded recovery command; --resume continues and the completed run leaves no journal; --resume with nothing to resume says so
facts.exit-codes: --help publishes all eleven codes with their meanings, and every member of the command's EXIT table is held to having one
facts.no-billable-provider: the canary is a seam and every case injects one; the real runner is never reached in a test, and the injected proof is derived from the preflight the command resolved
facts.mutations: 24 run locally on Windows across five sets, 23 killed, 1 survives (swallowing a preflight refusal, which this fixture cannot distinguish); each restored byte-identical by sha256
facts.full-suite-local: npm test on Windows: 1597 tests, 1592 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped
facts.ci-run: GitHub Actions run 35870095611 at bcfd79a, attempt 1, no job re-run, all four cells succeeded, 0 failures in any cell. Every earlier commit of this slice also passed all four cells: 35803035422 at 7d0d48a, the run at 0caaf7b, and 35860170561 at eeb79bc.
facts.live-tier: ubuntu-latest Node 24 cell only (job 107211621156), KILN_PI_COMPAT=live: 6 of 6 pass; skipped in the other three cells
facts.saved-credential: the canary request carries storedAuthPath for the agent directory the preflight resolved, and ONLY when the preflight found the stored file is what authenticates this selection: the canary refuses a stored path that is not there, and an environment-authenticated host commonly has no auth.json at all
facts.recovery-read: the journal is contained before the first byte — the state root must resolve inside the canonical project root and the journal inside that, as a regular file — validated against its schema before any field is used, and never the source of what is printed
facts.resume-command: RECOMPUTED FROM THIS RUN'S OWN PROJECT PATH, never taken from the journal it just read, and quoted for the shell it names: single quotes on Windows because PowerShell expands `$` and backticks inside double quotes (measured: "C:/a$null/project" arrives as C:/a/project), with an apostrophe written twice; single quotes elsewhere with the standard ''' sequence. The printed line says which shell it is for, since cmd.exe does not treat single quotes as quoting at all.
facts.resume-command-round-trip: the generated line is executed by the shell it names, against project paths holding $, a backtick, & and an apostrophe, and the path the command actually reached is read back out of its refusal — a string assertion that the path is wrapped in quotes cannot tell quoting that works from quoting that silently renames a directory

omissions.reason: The canary is the one step that sends a request to the selected provider, and the fixture's model is a real catalogue entry, so every case injects a runner. What a real canary does against a loopback provider is measured in test/live-canary.test.mjs and test/live-model-check.test.mjs.

An earlier zero-cost phase refuses first in this fixture, so a preflight that refuses cannot be told from one that is ignored through setup's own tests; the preflight's refusals are held by test/launch-checks.test.mjs.
R9 remains open: every content root other than <project>/planning-content is refused.
Setup supplies no custom credential declaration (D25, D13), and --local-state user refuses by name, so ACC-0085 stays not evaluated.

The stored-credential route could not be run end to end through setup without a billable provider: reaching the real canary with a built-in provider means its child resolves that provider's real endpoint, and setup supplies no custom provider configuration (D25). The wiring is asserted field by field on canaryRequest, and the stored-entry copy boundary is measured in test/pi-provider-canary.test.mjs.
